review_note:
Checked line by line: test file, helper-b31jo-oracle.R, manifest. All sha256 values (test, receipt, manifest, console log, helper, R sources) match the current files. The console log shows 140 passed, 0 failed, 0 skips, and 'Julia bridge: 10 live tests ran'. Counts reconcile by hand (5 intercept routes x 13 + 5 slope routes x 15 = 140). Totoro native rerun (taskset 280-285, one R process, nothing left running) gave 0 passed / 10 skipped because Totoro has no Julia. That confirms the skip guard but not the live counts, so live results rest on the Mac console log, which I did not rerun (no R on the Mac, per the rule).

Per family. (1) Gaussian and lognormal: agreement 1e-12 to 3e-11 against the exact Gaussian marginal (Gaussian) and an exact 1-D integral (lognormal). Julia is effectively exact here, so seed choice does not matter. Strongest rows. (2) Beta and Gamma, intercept and slope: agreement 2e-4 to 5.5e-4. The producer's six-seed scan, in scratchpad scan.out, shows Beta slope at the default SD (0.3) deviating 3.6e-3 to 8.9e-3 on all six draws. The fixture therefore also lowered the SD intercept to log(0.15). Gamma at 0.3 deviates 3e-4 to 1.2e-3. These deviations are systematic quadrature error of order 1e-3 to 1e-2, which is small against the emulated-bug gaps (0.75 to 17). I grant these rows only for likelihood assembly, selector alignment and SD-curve indexing at the fixtures (small-SD regime for Beta slope). A seed or SD level chosen to pass cannot support a quadrature-accuracy claim. (3) ZeroOneBeta, both rows: UNSUPPORTED. The producer reports a 3.07 log-likelihood departure from the exact marginal on one draw. The scratch diagnostic jo-ex6.R prints the 10.74 versus 7.67 comparison behind it, and I could not reproduce it because no live Julia ran here. The current fixture clamps interior y to [0.03, 0.97], which is fixture tuning, and the 12 clamped draws then agree to 7e-4 or better. A ledger row for ZOB would imply a route that can be wrong by about 3 log-likelihood units on ordinary data near the boundaries. The intercept route uses plain non-adaptive 32-node Gauss-Hermite (zeroonebeta.jl line 248), which fits the producer's explanation. I could not rule out the same weakness on the slope route (adaptive 11-point rule), so both rows are unlinked.

Other criteria. The oracles are hand-written base R, independent of the package: exact marginal or trapezoid integral with hand densities. Emulated bugs (swapped, sign-flipped and dropped selector, reversed non-palindromic SD vector, SD x2, slope SD on the intercept field) are asserted above 0.1 and observed at 0.75 or more (400x tolerance or more). The (1 | id) and (0 + x | id) formulas fit one independent scalar field each, matching the iid row layouts. A check that alpha plus/minus 0.1 does not raise the oracle confirms the optimum.

Does NOT establish: quadrature accuracy of Julia's iid routes on other draws or SD levels; anything for ZeroOneBeta on unclamped or boundary-heavy data; calibration, coverage, SEs or inference; native-versus-Julia parity (this is Julia against an oracle only); the DRM.jl source (only its head commit d5e3e6b11 is recorded, with no source hashes in the manifest); other seeds. The Beta slope grant is tied to the lowered SD level.
